scope.summary: Implement per-bone scale channels with child-propagation control per Section 13.18 (BK-18.1, TAI-BK-059), closing REQ-021: limb LENGTH and limb THICKNESS are independent parameters exposed as safe Skeletal channel axes (13.17 kind Skeletal), and scaling a parent never implicitly scales children unless the channel declares propagation — the proportion axes Daz relegates to third-party packs, native.
acceptance_criteria: BoneScaleChannel binds a Skeletal registry channel to (bone set, axis mode Length | Thickness | Uniform, propagate_to_children: bool); evaluation writes bone rest-transform scale without touching tissue deltas.
Propagation control proof: scaling thigh_l with propagate=false leaves calf_l/foot_l scale at 1.0; with propagate=true children follow — both asserted in one test.

Length vs thickness independence: a Length-mode scale changes bone length (joint-to-joint distance) with cross-section preserved; a Thickness-mode scale changes cross-section influence with length preserved (measured on the evaluated mesh).
Per-bone scale values flow into skinning as documented scale-aware transforms (no shear artifacts on a 2x length + 0.5x thickness fixture).

Existing skeletal channels (leg_length, hand_scale, shoulder_frame_width, torso_length) are re-bound through this lane so there is ONE skeletal scale mechanism (negative test: no second bespoke bone-scaling path).
scope.risk_if_missed: Without controlled per-bone scaling, long slender limbs (operator archetype) require morph hacks that fight skinning; implicit child propagation is how naive rigs turn a leg-length dial into a foot-size bug.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit skeleton and rigging

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
